findings.location: SPEC §1–3, especially “Current authority” and “Input, ownership and transport contract”; traceability O1/O25 and R1
findings.violated_obligation_or_claim: skill-write-specs rules 3–5 and operator message 192425 require an unresolved product/workflow choice to be asked rather than silently replacing the referenced proposal.
findings.observed_evidence: The assistant proposal specifies putting the model in Pi's terminal title. Message 192425 explicitly objects to pursuing an alternative. The SPEC instead mandates a new metadata protocol, asserts zero title writes, and labels O1 resolved even though no supplied operator message chooses metadata over title.
findings.failure_scenario: An engineer implements the extensive metadata producer/consumer and deployment state machinery, while the operator expected the documented title-extension proposal. The implementation can satisfy every listed test yet deliver an unapproved architecture and workflow.
findings.minimal_contract_correction: Record an explicit operator decision choosing title transport or metadata transport. Until then mark the specification BLOCKED, and do not present either alternative's dependent requirements as READY.

findings.location: R11 / AC-R11 / T2 and deployment preflight in R15/T4
findings.violated_obligation_or_claim: Each criterion must reach the shipped entry point and fail when the claimed outcome is absent.
findings.observed_evidence: R11 requires duplicate-publisher/preflight refusal, but AC-R11 assigns it to test:pi-title-resource-lifecycle under T2. Detecting another installed/active producer is a host inventory/preflight responsibility defined under R15/T4, not an intrinsic extension resource-lifecycle behavior.
findings.failure_scenario: A unit test supplies a duplicate-producer flag or fake refusal and passes, while the actual deployment preflight never inventories active producers; two extensions then publish the same source/pane metadata.
findings.minimal_contract_correction: Move duplicate-producer detection/refusal to AC-R15/T4 and require that test to invoke the shipped preflight inventory path. Keep AC-R11 limited to extension factory/session resource ownership.

findings.failure_scenario: The author can claim spec-audit success using any private script or static receipt; an independent reviewer cannot rerun the criterion or make it fail after a broken obligation/requirement mapping.
findings.minimal_contract_correction: Specify the exact read-only audit command, cwd, inputs and required output/exit status, or replace cmd:spec-audit with an honest fixed manual_by criterion naming the qualified reviewer and checklist.

findings.violated_obligation_or_claim: The obligation ledger must preserve actual source authority and must not invent inherited operator controls.
findings.observed_evidence: O22–O37 repeatedly cite “inherited control” not present in the 33 supplied operator messages. Several are canonical quality rules or prior-review conclusions; O26 converts a prior Opus review instruction into a detailed F1–F8/U1–U7/T1–T4 mandate. The current prompt explicitly identifies traceability as an author claim rather than authority.
findings.failure_scenario: Future implementers treat author/reviewer preferences and historical process artifacts as operator-approved product scope, obscuring which behavior can be changed only by the operator and making traceability appear complete when it is not.
findings.minimal_contract_correction: Reclassify every O22–O37 row to its actual source: direct message ID, named canonical rule, discovered fact, prior-review evidence, or non-authoritative author choice. Remove rows with no controlling obligation, and add any resulting unresolved operator decisions.

limitations: No host SSH, private API, credentials, transcripts, production configuration, live Pi session, reload, deployment or model selection was used, as required.
The native extension and feature tests do not exist; no claim is made that AC-R1–AC-R18 passed in implementation.
The one existing test run was constrained by the read-only sandbox: four tests failed on EPERM while creating temporary directories or Unix sockets. This proves neither product failure nor success.
Remote Alghul observations in packet receipts were checked for internal consistency and source provenance but could not be independently re-executed under the review boundary.
Routine unrelated helpers inside large support modules and unrelated changelog history were sampled; mandatory authority, obligation, requirement, criterion and task coverage was exhaustive.

The packet's official source documents are the pinned primary-source basis retrieved on 2026-10-08; their bytes matched the manifest.
The live worktree's uncommitted SPEC.md and traceability.json are the reviewed revision, not ancestor 6d3151132ffc0ecd2bc2f8fad01aee5661c940fd.
